A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fermat-state/IARO research despite the changed title. Their complete text, equations, 14 figures, three tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Level-Based Foraging and Overcooked experiments, option-count analyses, and appendix experiments on heterogeneous agents and eigenvector discovery.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, with revised Overcooked measurements in Figures 4 and 5.

M1.justification: The Fermat encoder, successor-distance learning, CMI regularization, ALLO eigenvector estimation, and option-training procedures are retained. Section 3.3 simplifies the formal definition of joint options, but the implemented full-team consensus requirement was already imposed in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three LBF configurations and three Overcooked scenarios, including the additional settings in Appendix A.4. The homogeneous grid demonstrations and two heterogeneous-agent scenarios in Appendix A.8 are also retained.

E2.justification: Figures 4 and 6 retain IQL, IPPO, VDN, MAPPO for LBF, IQL+Kron, IQL+RJS, and the scalar/multidimensional IARO comparison. Appendix A.9 retains the CEO comparison. No comparator is added or removed from the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1-3 retain the same transition counts, training budgets, option counts, preprocessing, architectures, and evaluation metrics. All three hyperparameter tables have unchanged entries. The revised Overcooked plots are not accompanied by a reported protocol change.

E4.justification: The existing Overcooked scalar-versus-multidimensional and option-count analyses have revised numerical evidence in Figures 4-5. Figure 5 reverses the ordering of the 10- and 15-option configurations. The analysis designs and other appendix diagnostics remain unchanged; no new ablation is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report IQM scores with 95% confidence intervals across 10 seeds for Figures 4 and 6. Figure 5 retains 15 seeds, 64 evaluation episodes, and standard-deviation error bars. Changed plotted uncertainty values do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: All five Overcooked panels in Figures 4-5 have substantially revised successful-delivery values. In Figure 4, final IQL+IARO values change from roughly 180 to 12 in Counter Circuit and 200 to 13 in Forced Coordination. Figure 5 also changes the 10-versus-15-option ordering, so this is not solely uniform rescaling. LBF plots and Appendix Figure 6 remain unchanged. These are revised reported results, not established performance losses.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the four-component joint-option definition, which explicitly included admissible agent subsets, with a three-component definition restricted to full-team options and distinguished from local options. This narrows the formal definition without changing the executed consensus procedure. The Fermat definitions and CMI proposition and proof are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the explicit hypothesis of discovering more diverse and generalisable coordination behaviours with a claim about better downstream performance. This modestly narrows the stated evaluation aim. The abstract and three principal contributions retain their substantive meaning.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 explicitly acknowledges that full-team consensus restricts behavioural expressivity and leaves subset-option integration to future work. The conclusion replaces the proposed relaxation of agent-state homogeneity with studying richer coordination topologies, while retaining the existing heterogeneous extension in Appendix A.8.

D1.justification: Appendix A.10 newly provides an IARO repository link for the proposed methods, baselines, and visualizations. v1 lacks this access statement. The implementation descriptions and hyperparameter values are otherwise substantially unchanged; the PDFs establish the new pointer, not independently verified repository contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds Boltianski, Martini, and Soltan's 1998 work as a source for the Fermat-set background in Section 2.3. Chen et al. (2022) receives additional explicit citations but was already discussed and evaluated in v1. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the introduction and joint-option discussion are edited, and Appendices A.3 and A.7 gain explanatory paragraphs about existing material. v3 also updates affiliation/publication text, corrects cross-references, and adds an LLM usage declaration in Appendix A.11. The main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The retained figures and tables are resized and redistributed under revised margins, heading styles, and colored citations. Figures 4-5 redraw the Overcooked vertical scales; Figures 6-7 now share a page. Table 3 moves beside Table 2 and receives a corrected Mac-DecPOMDP-training caption. The figure inventory and panel organization remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: v3 offers identifiable documentation gains through the code-access pointer, clearer consensus limitation, and additional algorithm explanations. However, the large revisions to the main Overcooked measurements, including a changed option-count ordering, are unexplained despite unchanged reported metrics and settings. The PDFs do not establish whether these revisions correct earlier errors or introduce reporting problems, so their impact on empirical accuracy and overall paper quality remains uncertain.
